If this answer satisfies your curiosity about my regard for you and your country then we can consider the meeting concluded unless you have another point to discuss with me."

After addressing the Lavian Representative Minister, he whispers to Minister Shari, "I saw his eyes shine, he is up to something."

(OOC: a little bit of background on the eyes shining part since its a piece of culture that's too obscure to just know. Some Iranic cultures consider shining eyes to be a sign of mischief.)[/quote]
Mr. Achebe nods and stands up, looking slightly disappointed at the quick and somewhat bitter end to the meeting. He seems to quickly remember something, picking up something off his chair and slightly examining it as the delegation stands up. "I wish to provide at least one positive piece of this visit." He holds out his hand, a leather case inside of it. "Produced here in Ijesa. It's part of the first production run as well, so its a bit of a collectors item."

The advisor stands up along with the governor and nods to the delegation. Thank you for coming sirs. I hope this wasn't considered too big of a waste of time."

[b]Ministry of Foreign Affairs[/b]
From: His Majesty, the King of the State of Ghazatna
To: His Excellency, the President of the State of God's Land

Your Excellency,

We address you with due respect, in light of the ongoing developments on the ground and the systematic colonial practices being carried out by individuals labeled as "civilians"while in reality, they actively engage in the dispossession of our people and the establishment of a forced reality at the expense of our historical and legitimate rights.

We affirm to Your Excellency that forced settlement, under any guise, is an act of aggression that violates the principles of international law and constitutes organized terrorism when practiced against a defenseless population whose land and resources are being seized by force.

Accordingly, we in the State of Ghazatna consider that those who steal land and settle on it under the protection of arms are not peaceful civilians, but colonial terrorists. We reserve our full right to confront them in a language they understandnamely, the right to legitimate self-defense by all means recognized under international law and the principles of justice.

We are not seeking escalation. However, we will never relinquish our rights nor allow our people to be stripped of their dignity and homeland under the false pretense of 'civility.' We hope you possess the political and moral courage to reassess this distorted reality.

With utmost respect,

His Majesty,
The King of the State of Ghazatna
